Beati qui esuriunt et sitiunt justitiam:
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for justice,
Blessed are the pure in heart,
for they shall be called sons of God.
Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter justitiam:
Blessed are those who endure persecution for the sake of justice,
for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Beati estis cum maledixerint vobis, et persecuti vos fuerint,
Blessed are you when they have slandered you, and persecuted you,
et dixerint omne malum adversum vos mentientes,
and spoken all kinds of evil against you, falsely,
quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cælis.
for your reward in heaven is plentiful.
Sic enim persecuti sunt prophetas, qui fuerunt ante vos.
For so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
You are the salt of the earth.
But if salt loses its saltiness,
with what will it be salted?
It is no longer useful at all,
You are the light of the world.
Non potest civitas abscondi supra montem posita,
A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden.
And they do not light a lamp
and put it under a basket,
ut luceat omnibus qui in domo sunt.
so that it may shine to all who are in the house.
Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus:
So then, let your light shine in the sight of men,
so that they may see your good works,
Nolite putare quoniam veni solvere legem aut prophetas:
Do not think that I have come to loosen the law or the prophets.
I have not come to loosen,
until heaven and earth pass away,
aut unus apex non præteribit a lege,
not one dot shall pass away from the law,
Qui ergo solverit unum de mandatis istis minimis,
whoever will have loosened one of the least of these commandments,
shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven.
But whoever will have done and taught these,
hic magnus vocabitur in regno cælorum.
such a one shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
quia nisi abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam scribarum et pharisæorum,
that unless your justice has surpassed that of the scribes
and the Pharisees you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to the ancients:
qui autem occiderit, reus erit judicio.
whoever will have murdered shall be liable to judgment.’
quia omnis qui irascitur fratri suo,
that anyone who becomes angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment.

Si ergo offers munus tuum ad altare,
Therefore, if you offer your gift at the altar,
et ibi recordatus fueris quia frater tuus habet aliquid adversum te:
and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
relinque ibi munus tuum ante altare,
leave your gift there, before the altar,
et vade prius reconciliari fratri tuo:

et tunc veniens offeres munus tuum.

Esto consentiens adversario tuo cito dum es in via cum eo:

ne forte tradat te adversarius judici,
lest perhaps the adversary may hand you over to the judge,

quia omnis qui viderit mulierem ad concupiscendum eam,

jam mœchatus est eam in corde suo.
has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
Quod si oculus tuus dexter scandalizat te,

expedit enim tibi ut pereat unum membrorum tuorum,

quam totum corpus tuum mittatur in gehennam.
than that your whole body be cast into Hell.

expedit enim tibi ut pereat unum membrorum tuorum,

quod autem his abundantius est, a malo est.

do not resist one who is evil,

qui solem suum oriri facit super bonos et malos: et pluit super justos et injustos.
